Wheeler's *it from bit* proposes that reality is informational all the way down: binary distinctions are fundamental, and spacetime and matter emerge from the relational structure of information processing. The picture has real purchase in physics (Shannon's [-@shannon1948] formalism, Landauer's [-@landauer1961] thermodynamic cost of erasure, information-theoretic reformulations of quantum mechanics) and none of it is in dispute. What is contested is the ontological inversion: the claim that information is more fundamental than the structural roles, that T, S, and Φ are emergent features of an information-processing substrate rather than conditions of what information consists in. T, S, and Φ are the three structural conditions whose necessity §2.8.5 declares, borne by Time, Space, and Substance. Three forms of the inversion follow. The replies test whether each can sustain the inversion without handing over what it meant to deflate.

*First.* The bit-first move holds that reality at the most fundamental level consists of bits (yes/no distinctions) with spacetime and matter emerging from their relational structure [@wheeler1990].

A bit requires difference to be a bit. Bateson's [-@bateson1972] phrase names the contrast at the core: information concerns a difference that can matter within some system. But Shannon's [-@shannon1948] formalism is deliberately abstract. Its sender, receiver, channel, and signal are formal roles in a communication model; the formalism by itself does not establish that every bit must have a physical bearer, spatial manifold, or temporal transmission. The stronger claim belongs only to physically realized information processing: where a difference is registered, propagated, or acted upon in a concrete system, there must be a persisting realization, distinguishable states, and an ordered process. That is a claim about realization, not a consequence of information theory alone. Information-theoretic foundationalism must therefore show how an abstract informational base is physically realized without already relying on the structural roles it proposes to derive.

*Second.* The Mathematical Universe Hypothesis [@tegmark2014] goes further: reality does not resemble mathematics but is a mathematical structure, and all mathematically consistent structures equally exist.

For a mathematical structure to be a structure at all, its elements must stand in determinate relations. That directly supports a role of differentiation. It does not follow from determinate relatedness alone that the relations are asymmetric, temporally ordered, continuous, or borne by a concrete substance. Those further roles enter only when the mathematical structure is claimed to be concretely realized or dynamically operative. Tegmark's own account requires the mathematical structure to be the kind of thing whose elements stand in determinate relations; this concedes the roles at the level of what a mathematical structure consists in. The plenitude reading compounds the concession: every mathematically consistent structure instantiates the roles under abstraction. The Platonist has not escaped Time, Space, or Substance. They hold mathematical structure together.

What the section's account requires Tegmark to give up is not the mathematical-identity thesis as such but its unrestricted plenitude complement. The Mathematical Universe Hypothesis at Level IV holds that all mathematically consistent structures equally exist (*Our Mathematical Universe* [-@tegmark2014]). If T∧S∧Φ are necessary conditions for a mathematical structure to be concretely real rather than merely abstractly consistent, then the Level IV plenitude is structurally bounded: only T∧S∧Φ-consistent structures are candidates for physical instantiation. The section's claim is not that MUH is false but that it requires the structural conditions as a constraint on plenitude. Tegmark's account can absorb T, S, and Φ as specifying what it takes for a consistent structure to be physically instantiated; the cost is giving up the claim that mathematical consistency alone is sufficient for physical existence.

*Third.* The computational-universe move presses the cleanest form. @lloyd2006 holds that the universe is a quantum computer: physical processes are computations, particles are data, interactions are logic gates. @deutsch1997 and @wolfram2002 develop parallel variants. The common commitment is that computation precedes the structural roles ontologically.

A physically realized computation instantiates each of the three roles at the level of the computing. For a bit to be processed in a concrete machine, there must be an ordered transition between states through a medium capable of realizing it; this supplies the relevant temporal role. An abstract computation, considered only as a mathematical mapping, does not by itself establish physical succession. For information to be held, maintained, and updated, something must persist as the being that bears the informational state, that *is* Substance. For bits to be distinct from one another, there must be relational non-identity among them, that *is* Space. A computation lacking any of the three is not a computation but something weaker: a static set of symbols (no Time), a dynamic flux with no being (no Substance), or a homogeneous stream with no distinguishable units (no Space). Landauer's [-@landauer1961] principle cuts the same way from physics: erasing a bit costs kT ln 2 of energy (the Landauer limit, where k is Boltzmann's constant and T is temperature, the minimum thermodynamic cost of erasing one bit), and thermodynamic cost requires a physical substrate with temporal evolution, spatial distinctness of states, and persistent beings.

A kindred deflation drops the computational framing entirely for ontic structural realism: @ladymanRoss2007 argue that only relational structure is fundamental and relata are ontologically dispensable. Structure, on this view, goes all the way down, with no bearer beneath it. This form of the inversion has to be met head-on rather than deflected, because the case against it is the case for Φ.

Structure is not a thing; structure is what things have. A pattern is always a pattern *of* something, as ownership is always ownership *of* something and a dent is always a dent *in* something. "Structure all the way down" asks us to keep the having while dismissing everything that has: to keep the floor plan after demolishing the building. But the structure of a building is not a second object standing alongside it; subtract the building and no structure is left over, only a blueprint, and a blueprint is a *description* of a building rather than a building.

The structural realist has a reply: the relata are nothing but nodes in the structure. A "thing" just is a position in the pattern, with no nature of its own. But a node is still a something. To be a position is to be the position *of* something positioned; relocating the bearer into the word "node" does not abolish it, it renames it. Nor does multiple realizability help: that one structure can be built in steel, wood, or concrete shows it independent of any *particular* material, not independent of material *as such*. A blueprint realizable in many media is still a sheet of paper until it is built in some medium or other. The dispute reduces to a single question: can anything be *exhausted* by its relations, with no nature of its own beneath how it relates? If not, then under every structure there is at least a minimal what-it-is that the structure is the structure *of*, and that is Φ. This is the intrinsic nature Russellian monism locates beneath physical structure (§4.3.3), and it is the precise point on which the present account parts from the structuralism of §4.3.9. Relational structure without anything across which relations obtain is ∅ (the Null State, the configuration in which none of T, S, or Φ is instantiated), foreclosed in §2.7.

*The Concession Move.* One last move remains to the opponent: not denial, but concession, that information is the substrate, and what the argument calls Time, Space, and Substance are already informational through and through. Look at the words information theory reaches for when it needs to name where information lives. Channel. Bearer. Register. Substrate. Carrier. Medium. Every one is a word for something. Information is descriptive. It needs something to describe.

Information requires distinction to be information; transition requires succession to be transition; processing requires persistence to be processing. Strip the roles and what remains is not a more fundamental informational substrate but ∅. Wheeler's slogan, on the present account, runs in both directions: it comes from bit only where bit is already the output of T, S, and Φ doing their work. The unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics in describing physical structure (which *it from bit* implicitly trades on) is taken up directly at §4.3.6.

*What converges.* Five moves, five concessions. A bit requires difference to be a bit: a difference that makes a difference is already three, distinction (Space), being and medium (Substance), and directed registration (Time). A mathematical structure requires determinate relations among its elements and therefore supports the difference-role. The temporal and bearer roles require an additional realization premise; mathematical consistency or plenitude alone does not supply them. Computation instantiates each role at the level of the computing: temporal evolution, persistent beings, distinct units, with Landauer's principle recording the thermodynamic cost of that instantiation. Ontic structural realism drops the bearer and keeps the pattern, and a pattern is a pattern of something: the node it relocates the bearer into is still a something. The retreat to information-as-substrate names every locale of information in structural vocabulary (channel, bearer, register, medium) and adds a fifth instance of the same concession.
